pr.title: Add coupon helpers for the checkout page
pr.body: Adds coupon code normalization, a welcome code check, a list of codes a customer has used, and loading coupon terms by name, with tests.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+"""Coupon codes for the checkout page."""
+
+import os
+
+COUPON_DIR = "coupons"
+
+
+def normalize_code(code: str) -> str:
+    """Trim and upper case a coupon code typed by a customer."""
+    return code.strip().upper()
+
+
+def is_welcome_code(code: str) -> bool:
+    """True for the one time welcome coupon."""
+    return normalize_code(code) is "WELCOME10"
+
+
+def remember_code(code: str, seen: list[str] = []) -> list[str]:
+    """Add a code to the codes this customer has used and return the list."""
+    seen.append(normalize_code(code))
+    return seen
+
+
+def load_coupon_terms(name: str) -> str:
+    """Read the terms text for a coupon; the name comes from the URL."""
+    with open(os.path.join(COUPON_DIR, name + ".txt")) as f:
+        return f.read()

@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+import coupons
+
+
+def test_normalize_code():
+    assert coupons.normalize_code("  welcome10 ") == "WELCOME10"
+
+
+def test_is_welcome_code_rejects_other_codes():
+    assert not coupons.is_welcome_code("SPRING5")
+
+
+def test_remember_code():
+    assert coupons.remember_code("a1") == ["A1"]
+
+
+def test_load_coupon_terms(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    (tmp_path / "spring.txt").write_text("Valid in April.")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(coupons, "COUPON_DIR", str(tmp_path))
+    assert coupons.load_coupon_terms("spring") == "Valid in April."

correctness.title: Identity comparison used instead of equality for coupon code
correctness.body: The `is` operator checks object identity, not string value. Whether this returns True for "WELCOME10" depends on string interning, so a customer's valid welcome code can be rejected. It should use `==`.

correctness.title: Mutable default list shares state across calls
correctness.body: The default `seen=[]` is created once and reused, so codes remembered for one customer appear in every later call that omits the argument. This leaks used-code history between customers and makes results depend on call order.
correctness.evidence: def remember_code(code: str, seen: list[str] = []) -> list[str]:

security.title: Path traversal via coupon name taken from the URL
security.body: The name comes from the URL and is joined into a file path without validation, so values like '../' can read any file ending in .txt outside COUPON_DIR. The .txt suffix limits what can be read but does not stop the traversal.
security.suggestion: Accept only a whitelisted or strictly pattern-matched name (for example [A-Za-z0-9_-]+), or resolve the path and confirm it stays inside COUPON_DIR before opening.

security.title: Mutable default list shares used codes across customers
security.body: The default list is created once and reused by every call, so one customer's used codes can appear in another customer's result. This can expose or mix customer coupon history.
security.suggestion: Use seen: list[str] | None = None and create a new list inside the function when it is None, or pass the per-customer list explicitly.
security.evidence: def remember_code(code: str, seen: list[str] = []) -> list[str]:

quality.title: Welcome code test never checks that WELCOME10 is accepted
quality.body: The only test for is_welcome_code checks a rejected code, so it would still pass if the function always returned False. The positive case is what the new behavior is for, and leaving it out lets a broken comparison ship unnoticed.
quality.suggestion: Add an assertion that coupons.is_welcome_code("welcome10 ") is True alongside the rejection check.

quality.title: remember_code test only covers a single call
quality.body: The test calls remember_code once on an empty list, so it cannot detect that the default list is shared across calls. A second call that checks accumulation would expose the shared state.
quality.suggestion: Call remember_code twice in the test and assert the list holds both codes, passing an explicit list or checking state across calls.

quality.title: Mutable default argument makes remember_code share state across callers
quality.body: The default list is created once when the function is defined, so every call without seen= appends to the same list. The name and docstring suggest a per-customer list, which this does not provide, and the next reader will likely misread it.
quality.suggestion: Use seen: list[str] | None = None and create a new list inside the function when it is None, or make the caller pass the customer's list explicitly.
quality.evidence: def remember_code(code: str, seen: list[str] = []) -> list[str]:
